statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory use of French language and Latin alphabet; company names must comply with French orthographic rules and cannot be misleading or infringe protected terms
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Protected corporate titles (e.g., 'banque', 'assurance', 'courtage') requiring prior ministerial approval
Geographical or historical terms without authorization
Words likely to confuse the public regarding activity or capital
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within two months of official rejection notice, file administrative appeal directly with the greffe du tribunal de commerce; upon adverse decision, possible judicial review before the administrative tribunal or Conseil d'État

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for new entities; unannounced inspections by greffe or tax authorities occur in approximately 5-10% of cases involving complex or high-risk structures

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book I and Book II: Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-10, L. 221-1 to L. 227-27 (SAS-specific provisions), R. 227-1 to R. 227-15; Council Regulation (EU) 2021/1139 for maritime sector where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) having jurisdiction over the registered office; filings are administered through the electronic single window (Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 – Déclaration de constitution de société (immatriculation au RCS); accompanied by the signed Articles of Association (statuts constitutifs), legal publication certificate (certificat de parution), and capital deposit certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists for an SAS; the stated capital may be as low as EUR 1. If cash contributions are used, the full amount must be subscribed and deposited in escrow with a French credit institution, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary. The escrow is released to the company upon issuance of the RCS registration certificate (extrait Kbis).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [SAS NAME]: RESOLVED, that the incorporation subscriptions have been wholly made and the contributions paid, deposited in escrow as required by law, and such subscriptions are ratified. RESOLVED, that the registered office is adopted at [ADDRESS] within the jurisdiction of the Registrar of the Commercial Court, and all statutory books and documents shall be kept there. RESOLVED, that [NAME] is appointed as Chairman of the SAS with full power to bind the company in all acts within its corporate purpose. RESOLVED, that the Chairman is authorized to complete the application for registration with the RCS and to take any ancillary steps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitution and signature of the Articles of Association (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders and, where applicable, a French notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding shareholders shall agree on the company name, corporate object (ISIC 5222 offshore towage and salvage), share capital, registered office, governance rules, and first Chairman. The statuts may be executed by private deed unless any non-cash contribution consists of real property or a going concern, in which case a notarial act is mandatory. Each shareholder signs and accepts the statuts; any special valuations for in-kind contributions must be annexed.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (statuts)
List of shareholders with share subscriptions
Valuation report (rapport du commissaire aux apports) if in-kind contributions exist
Acceptance letter of the first Chairman
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Material omissions are cured by a supplementary amendment (acte rectificatif) and re-signature; a refusal of signature can be resolved through additional notarial advice and execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal formation notice in an authorized legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) licensed in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the statuts are signed, cause a mandatory legal notice containing the corporate name, legal form (SAS), share capital, registered office, corporate object, duration, and Chairman's name to be published in a licensed JAL. Obtain the certificate of publication (certificat de parution) and include it in the filing dossier; the notice must appear before the RCS application is submitted.
required_dossiers: Signed statuts
Identity details of the Chairman and directors
Capital subscription statement
Registered office address and competent court jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, request a corrected attestation from the same JAL and re-file with updated dates; an incorrect notice is cured by publishing a second corrective notice and attaching both certificates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit confirmation and escrow blocking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or notaire holding escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All cash contributions must be deposited into a temporary or escrow account in France; the depositary issues an attestation of funds blocked until the company is registered. The deposit certificate must state the total amount, the depositor, the bank/notary identity, and the designated future account of the SAS. The funds are released automatically upon presentation of the Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Proof of deposit (certificat de consignation des fonds or attestation de blocage)
Copy of the share capital clause from the statuts
Bank account or notary escrow reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is incomplete, ask the depositary to reissue; if a bank refuses, use a notary or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations to receive and hold the funds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration application through the electronic single window
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) transmitting to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the electronic single window and complete the standardized Form M0 declaration. Attach the signed statuts, legal notice certificate, capital deposit certificate, identity and eligibility documents of the Chairman and beneficial owners, and proof of registered office address. Pay the statutory registry filing fees online and submit; the system routes the dossier to the RCS of the relevant court.
required_dossiers: Form M0 data entry
Signed Articles of Association (statuts)
Legal publication certificate
Capital deposit certificate
Identity documents of Chairman and directors
Declaration of non-conviction under French law
Proof of registered office address (lease, ownership deed, or domiciliation agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a deficiency notice or payment requirement, the applicant has 15 days to respond online with corrective documents; rejection is fully cured by timely supplementing the file and resubmitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of RCS registration certificate (extrait Kbis)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After successful verification of the dossier, the Greffe issues the official Kbis extract, assigns the SIREN/SIRET identifiers, and triggers publication in the Bulletin Officiel des Annonces Civiles et Commerciales (BODACC). The Kbis constitutes legal proof of the company's existence and corporate powers.
required_dossiers: Receipt of the application from the Guichet unique
Proof of payment of registry fees
Any responses to RCS observations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis extract contains errors, file a rectification request with the Greffe; a formal refusal of registration can be challenged before the competent commercial court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF, French tax office (Service des Impôts des Entreprises), and Direction départementale des territoires et de la mer / DGAMPA for maritime compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with URSSAF as an employer, open a permanent corporate bank account, subscribe hull and machinery and protection and indemnity insurance, and notify the maritime administration of the company's operational intent. If a tug or salvage vessel is to be flagged in France, initiate the vessel registration and safety certification with the competent maritime authorities.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
Business bank account details
Insurance placement certificates (P&I, hull, liability)
Vessel registration and safety inspection dossier if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If post-registration registrations are delayed, use the Guichet unique to chase the CFE, or contact URSSAF directly to obtain temporary employer numbers; any administrative refusal can be remedied by providing additional Kbis and company documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Affaires Maritimes, de la Pêche et de l'Aquaculture (DGAMPA) under the Ministry of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion; operational control delegated to the Direction Interrégionale de la Mer (DIRM) and the relevant maritime Prefectural authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation/agrément d'exploitation d'opérations de remorquage et d'assistance maritime dans les eaux sous juridiction française (Authorization to carry out marine towage and salvage operations in French waters).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) – Inspectorate of Classified Environmental Facilities (ICPE), in coordination with the maritime administration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – Environmental Impact Registration (EER) with streamlined assessment; no full EIA is required for the company's headquarters or administrative office. For each operational tug/salvage vessel, a vessel-specific environmental compliance checklist applies under MARPOL and French environmental protection articles; a full environmental impact assessment may be required only for wreck removal involving seabed disturbance in vulnerable marine zones.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with MARPOL Annexes I, II, V and VI, French Decree 2001-254 and Order of 10 March 2004; no oily or chemical discharge within 12 nautical miles of the French coast and only through approved reception facilities anywhere within French jurisdictional waters; sulphur content of marine fuels limited to 0.5% m/m globally and 0.1% m/m in Sulfur Emission Control Areas (SECAs); nitrogen oxides (NOx) per Tier III limits in emission control areas; wastewater sludge and hazardous waste must be transferred to certified shore-based treatment facilities; vessels conduct waste logbook reporting and submit annual emissions and fuel consumption data to the maritime authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for any shore installations under the local fire service (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours – SDIS); structural load inspection of quayside or warehouse facilities where applicable; workplace health and safety clearance via the Labour Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail) and compliance with the French Labour Code and ILO Maritime Labour Convention 2006; survival, lifesaving, and salvage firefighting equipment onboard must carry valid classification society certificates (e.g., Bureau Veritas) and be approved in the vessel safety certificate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), including the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE) for eligible non-established businesses. Principal online portals are impots.gouv.fr for tax administration and formal tax filings, and the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated through the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI) for entity registration formalities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS obtains its SIREN and SIRET identifiers through the INPI Guichet unique upon incorporation. The DGFiP then assigns or confirms the French tax account and corporate income tax registration. A French VAT identification number is requested from the competent SIE, generally after incorporation and before commencing taxable transactions requiring VAT registration. The VAT number normally comprises the country prefix FR, a two-digit control key, and the entity's nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity carrying on taxable activities in France must register with the SIEE or the relevant competent tax office, submit identification and constitutional documents, evidence of business activity, bank and representative details where applicable, and obtain a French VAT number. A non-EU business generally must appoint a French tax representative unless an applicable statutory exemption or mutual-assistance arrangement applies. EU-established businesses may register directly without a French fiscal representative, subject to the applicable VAT rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Certain SASs may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime for up to five fiscal years if the statutory eligibility conditions are satisfied, including qualifying ownership, activity, age, and size requirements. This is not a general United States-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement the EU ATAD II framework and can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or otherwise neutralize outcomes involving hybrid entities, instruments, or permanent establishments. The election must be made within the statutory period and notified to the competent tax authority.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France does not provide a general VAT-registration threshold for non-established businesses making taxable supplies in France; registration and VAT accounting may be required from the first taxable transaction. For French-established businesses using the domestic franchise en base de TVA, the principal turnover thresholds are generally EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and specified equivalent activities and EUR 37,500 for services, subject to statutory tolerance thresholds, activity-specific rules, and legislative changes. Businesses exceeding the applicable franchise thresholds must transition to normal VAT obligations. Cross-border B2B services and transactions subject to reverse charge can create filing obligations even where no French VAT is collected.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting through approved platforms or the public invoicing portal framework. The regime is not a universal real-time pre-clearance system. Mandatory receipt of electronic invoices is scheduled for all businesses from 1 September 2026. Mandatory issuance is scheduled from 1 September 2026 for large and medium-sized businesses and from 1 September 2027 for small and micro-enterprises, subject to the applicable legal timetable. Electronic invoices must use an approved structured or hybrid format and contain required invoice data. E-reporting of relevant B2C and cross-border transactions will apply according to the statutory timetable. Businesses must maintain reliable digital records, VAT ledgers, and audit trails; no general digital tax stamp is required for every invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from the European Union to destinations outside the EU may be exempt from French VAT with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the supplier establishes that the goods left the EU customs territory and satisfies the documentary and invoicing requirements. For towage and salvage, services are not automatically zero-rated merely because they are performed offshore or involve a foreign customer. B2B services are generally located under the customer-location rule and may be subject to reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction. Specific French VAT exemptions may apply to services directly required for qualifying sea-going vessels engaged in international navigation, including qualifying towing, salvage, and related services, provided the statutory vessel, use, contractual, and documentary conditions are met. Services connected with vessels or operations that do not satisfy those conditions require transaction-by-transaction analysis. VAT refunds require valid invoices, eligible business expenditure, and evidence that the input tax relates to taxable or exempt-with-credit activities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration accepted by French customs or the competent EU customs system, including the Movement Reference Number where applicable
Export accompanying document and customs exit confirmation or equivalent proof that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice, contract, packing list, and transport documentation appropriate to the transaction
Bill of lading, sea waybill, charter-party evidence, or other maritime transport record where relevant
Proof of delivery or destination outside the EU where required to substantiate export status

For qualifying vessel-related exemptions, vessel registration and classification evidence, proof of international-navigation status, service orders, work reports, and evidence that the services were directly required for the vessel or its cargo
Customer VAT identification and reverse-charge evidence for applicable B2B services
Banking and payment records supporting the underlying transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not a generally mandatory French export-VAT document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export-VAT qualification. The taxpayer must retain reliable evidence supporting the VAT treatment and produce it during a DGFiP or customs audit. Unsupported exemption or zero-rating may be reassessed as French VAT, generally at the applicable rate, with recovery of wrongly deducted input VAT, late-payment interest, and tax penalties. Penalties may include a percentage surcharge for insufficient or inaccurate filings, increased sanctions for deliberate or fraudulent conduct, and customs penalties for false declarations or failure to substantiate export. Criminal liability may arise in cases involving intentional tax fraud, forged documents, concealment, or organized fraudulent schemes. The precise assessment depends on the nature of the error, taxpayer conduct, cooperation, limitation periods, and applicable customs or tax provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Central Bank of France) with the Direction des Statistiques Monétaires et de la Balance des Paiements responsible for foreign-exchange statistics, and the Direction Générale du Trésor of the French Ministry of Economy, Finance and Sovereign Industrial and Digital Sovereignty acting as the principal financial regulator for capital movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a euro-zone jurisdiction with fully convertible capital and current accounts. No exchange-control approval or treasury licence is required for ordinary commercial payments, profit remittances, or capital operations under the Code monétaire et financier. The only material compliance obligations are statistical declaration to the Banque de France through resident banking intermediaries, EU/OECD capital freedom requirements, potential scrutiny under the French outward-direct-investment screening regime in strategic sectors, and post-event reporting for direct investment flows exceeding administrative thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion into euros in France. Export revenues may be retained in any currency in resident bank accounts. However, all cross-border transactions are subject to balance-of-payments reporting by the resident bank to the Banque de France, and the exporter must maintain underlying contracts, invoices, import-export documents, and bank records for the statutory six-year limitation period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account and Treasury Liquidity Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (Crédit Agricole CIB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Structured Marine Finance Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. (via Natixis for international banking services)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: French Interbank payment institutions and electronic money institutions may offer operational e-current accounts and cross-border usance payment rails, but comprehensive viability is Medium with restrictive use for capital escrow and high-value salvage settlements. An EMI can support routine operational payments, but tier-1 regulated commercial banks remain mandatory for capital injection escrow accounts, documentary letters of credit, and treasury hedging activities. EMIs generally lack the correspondent banking depth, documentary credit issuance authority, and Lloyd's-form escrow acceptance infrastructure required in an offshore towage and salvage contract flow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and Ultimate Beneficial Owners of the SAS must ordinarily appear physically at a French branch or at a notary-public appointment to complete the high-risk KYC interview, particularly when the business scope is maritime salvage and towage and any director is a non-resident. Some tier-1 banks may permit whole-bank remote opening using a certified video identification process authorised by ACPR/AMF, but in practice for a Medium-Risk_Enhanced profile with emergency salvage operations, the physical-presence mandate is the default and safest onboarding path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO (Ultimate Beneficial Owner) situated in a non-cooperative jurisdiction or an offshore financial centre without economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete UBO chain with passport copies, physical address proof, certificate of incorporation for every intermediate entity, a group structural diagram, mandatory French UBO declaration recorded in the Corporate Registry, and a professional banking reference from a respected European institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border wires to unpredictable counterparties (shipowners, port agents, salvors) without pre-reconciliation of underlying contracts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Master Towage and Salvage Agreements, Lloyd's Standard Form of Salvage Agreement (LOF 2011), voyage and towage data (AIS-logs, master's reports), itemised salvage invoices, pre-notified wire transfer settlement matrix, and a standing instruction protocol for emergency disbursements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between declared accounting turnover and wire-flow volumes caused by emergency payments for bunkers, tugs, port charges and salvage awards
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French statutory audited financial statements, an independent accountant's confirmation of revenue recognition, historical bank transaction registers, custodial escrow agreements, asset registry for tug vessels, and contemporaneous boarding or job-sheet records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Involvement of sanctioned sovereign waters or counterparties in emergency search and salvage operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A third-party sanctions screening result from a reputable provider, an end-user / end-owner declaration, insurance certificates covering wreck removal and salvage, flag-state authorisation, U.S. OFAC and EU sanctions self-declaration, and an exclusion of any blocked vessel or port in the charter party.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections to the French SAS must be executed via SWIFT MT103 in EUR to the dedicated capital escrow account opened in the name of the company, with field 70 'Remittance Information' stating clearly 'CAPITAL INCREASE / APP' and the share-subscription reference. The remitter must provide the subscribing deed, minutes of the shareholders' meeting or board resolution, the notarised or certified capital increase statement, and proof of legitimacy of funds for a complete restriction-free credit. French resident banks must capture the economic purpose code for balance-of-payments statistics, and any individual transaction of at least EUR 10,000 triggers automatic anti-money-laundering verification and TRACFIN notification obligations. Required supporting documents include the updated Kbis extract, SIRET number, UBO declaration, and evidence that the capital deposit is not originating from an unlicensed or opaque arrangement incompatible with EU anti-money-laundering rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 for immediate wire settlements when the disbursement exceeds the bank's online banking limits, and documentary USANCE or sight letter of credit (Lettres de Crédit Documentaires) executed under UCP600 for non-immediate or escrowed marine salvage awards. For emergency towage and salvage disbursements, payment can be transmitted through the bank's high-velocity euro rail (European SEPA Credit Transfer or SWIFT EUR single-euro area) with real-time liquidity management. The settlement platform must support Lloyd's Standard Form of Salvage Agreement provisions; specifically, security to the salvors via bank guarantee or escrow is often required before the release of ship or cargo, and the bank should allow the making of an escrow account deed with multiple-security interests under French law.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign-exchange forwards and non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with French credit institutions for hedging commercial foreign-currency exposures directly arising from tug invoices and salvage awards in currencies such as USD and GBP.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps and FX swaps for managing matched funding and large marine-asset capital leases in foreign currencies.
Premium-bearing foreign-exchange options and zero-cost collars covering the residual FX exposure of receivables receivable in volatile emerging-market currencies.
Commodity-linked hedging is permitted only when directly incident to the fuel-oil and bunker-cost exposure of the towing fleet.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts (balance sheet, income statement, notes) filed with the Trade and Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, shareholder approval and deposit must both occur by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered coercive fine (astreinte), registry non-compliance notice, and after a formal injunction, risk of judicial dissolution and strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Cerfa 2065-series / liasse fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end: the second business day after 1 May; for any other fiscal year-end: within three months of the fiscal-year close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5% of unpaid tax if corrected within 30 days, 10% after formal notice, 40% in bad faith, 80% in cases of deliberate tax evasion; plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.2%

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a SAS that exceeds at fiscal year-end at least two of the three thresholds: total assets greater than EUR 4 million, net turnover greater than EUR 8 million, or an average permanent workforce greater than 50 employees; group-supervision thresholds may also apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Règlement ANC No. 2014-03, as amended) for individual statutory accounts; EU-adopted IFRS is permitted for consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO re-filing is prescribed. The UBO register must be declared at incorporation and updated within 30 days of any change in direct or indirect beneficial ownership of more than 25% of share capital or voting rights. During the annual accounts approval process, the legal representative must verify and advise the Greffe of any shareholding or beneficial-ownership changes that occurred during the year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 600 per year for a standard registered-office / domiciliation service in France (typical market range for an SAS)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 15,000 per year for a statutory audit by a licensed commissaire aux comptes for a small or mid-size SAS

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No broad statutory tax holidays; specific preferential deductions include 100% R&D expensing, innovation tax credit (up to 30% of eligible costs), and accelerated depreciation for maritime equipment

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultat (Formulaire 1200) via official electronic portal impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15th day of the 4th month following fiscal year-end (e.g., 15 April for 31 December fiscal year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net turnover from towage and salvage services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report standalone or consolidated revenue; non-residents without PE appoint fiscal representative

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after deductions and TP adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply arm's length adjustments; non-residents file via representative if no French PE

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.5% of tax due per month of delay (capped at 25%); 40€ daily surcharge after 45 days; criminal penalties for evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Tax Residency Certificate and application form (via impots.gouv.fr or tax office) to claim reduced DTA rates
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0%-10% (typically 5% under DTAs); Interest: 0%-10% (often exempt under EU rules or treaties)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 in related-party transactions triggering Local File / Master File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France enforces OECD-aligned ESR; active maritime operations generally meet substance requirements, though IP holding entities require compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to declare revenue or understate profits from salvage contracts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to 80% of evaded tax; civil restitution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, imprisonment, and management disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining SAS without genuine French business operations for towage activities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transaction recharacterization, back taxation with penalties up to 500% of evaded tax, potential dissolution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil piercing; personal restitution and possible prison sentences

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform due diligence or file suspicious transaction reports on cross-border payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 1 million or 5% of annual turnover; maritime license suspension
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, disqualification, and criminal charges

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inadequate TP documentation or incorrect arm's length pricing for related-party contracts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP adjustments increasing taxable base by 100% of adjustment; penalties up to 80% of additional tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and potential imprisonment for fraudulent practices

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Comply with Double Tax Agreement Relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Improper denial or misuse of treaty benefits for royalty or interest payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional withholding tax, penalties up to 40% of unpaid tax; possible criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal restitution liability and administrative sanctions including professional activity bans
